data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's central syllogism is self-defeating: it defines 'frontier' via mutual exclusion (at least one critic must reject it), then treats the §11.3 flag—whose meaning is precisely the point at issue—as proof that the claim reached the frontier. That is circular: the conclusion (frontier status) is established by re-labeling the very signal the problem asked the target to justify. The target thus presupposes what it purports to demonstrate, so the flag is sustained on a pretext, not by adjudication.
